title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1976 divided-power De Rham notes surrounding it. It is page 137 of the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §11, which deals with the pairing on groups of connected components of Néron models. It is evidently misfiled, or reused as scrap paper, in cote 136.

Setting: S is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring, K its fraction field, s its closed point. A_K is an abelian variety with dual A'_K, and A, A' are their Néron models. Φ_0 and Φ'_0 are the groups of components of the special fibres, and Φ_0(ℓ) is the ℓ-primary part. M and M' are the character groups of the tori in the special fibres of the connected Néron models; M_ℓ and M'_ℓ are their ℓ-adic or ℓ-divisible versions. The monodromy pairing (9.1.2) gives a map ũ_ℓ : M_ℓ → Ṁ'_ℓ into the dual of M'_ℓ.

Theorem 11.5. Assume S is henselian and A_K has semistable reduction. Then the ℓ-part of the component group is the special fibre of coker(ũ_ℓ): Φ_0(ℓ) ≅ Φ(ℓ) ×_S s.

Applying the theorem to A'_K, and using the compatibility (10.2.2) of the monodromy pairing with transposition, gives Φ'_0(ℓ) ≅ coker(ᵗũ_ℓ) ×_S s. Since the cokernels of a map and of its transpose between dual lattices are canonically Pontryagin dual (via Ext), one obtains the perfect pairing (11.4.1) Φ_0(ℓ) × Φ'_0(ℓ) → Q/Z. This is Grothendieck's pairing, i.e. his conjecture 11.3 in the semistable case.

Remark 11.5.2:
(a) The theorem implies ũ_ℓ is an isogeny, i.e. u_ℓ is non-degenerate ('séparant'), even for ℓ = p, where this does not follow trivially from the definition in 9.6. The proof does not use the deeper Theorem 10.4.
(b) Using 10.4, which gives an integral monodromy pairing u : M ⊗ M' → Z_S, one sets Φ = coker(ũ : M → Ṁ'). The page breaks off here; in SGA 7 the text continues by identifying Φ_0 with Φ_s globally, which is the Raynaud/Grothendieck description of component groups via the monodromy pairing.

The argument serves the proof of the perfectness of Grothendieck's pairing on component groups for semistable abelian varieties.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. 'résulte immédiatement la définition d'un accouplement parfait' should be read as: the existence (construction) of the perfect pairing 11.4.1 follows. The wording is slightly loose but not wrong.

ideas.what: Component group of the Néron model of a semistable abelian variety equals the cokernel of the map induced by the monodromy pairing on character groups (ℓ-adically, including ℓ = p)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's description of Φ via the monodromy pairing (SGA 7 IX Thm 11.5)

ideas.what: Perfectness of the pairing Φ_0 × Φ'_0 → Q/Z in the semistable case, deduced by applying the theorem to the dual abelian variety and transposing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 IX); general case studied by Bégueri, McCallum, Bertapelle–Bosch, Suzuki

ideas.what: Non-degeneracy of the ℓ-adic monodromy pairing, including ℓ = p, without using Theorem 10.4
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, Remarque 11.5.2 a)

missed.claim: Archival note only, with no mathematical novelty: this sheet is a page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript, misfiled (or reused as scrap paper) within the 1975–76 divided-power De Rham notes of cote 136.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant for cataloguing: the page is part of the SGA 7 manuscript, not of the De Rham conference notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is verbatim published SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, Theorem 11.5 and Remark 11.5.2, well known and credited to Grothendieck.
